subject: Post-call: POC decision log — regional token budget & model fallback matrix
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria@lexicon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: POC decision log — regional token budget & model fallback matrix

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. High-level ask from Lexicon: 3-week POC to validate multi-lingual extraction + generation for EU legal templates with strict latency and hallucination guardrails. Key points below and an action table at the end.

Summary of decisions from call:
- Scope: 3-week POC focused on Spanish, German, and French flows (customer-facing templates + admin edits).
- Success criteria: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on sample prompts; generation hallucination rate < 3% (manual spot-check protocol); p50 latency < 220ms; stable throughput 10 qps.
- Model shortlist (initial): Mistral-Instruct-34B (primary), Llama-3-13B-quant (fallback trimmed), and a lightweight opt-2.7b for degraded mode. We proposed tokenized QA + reranking to reduce hallucinations.
- Regional token budget constraint: Lexicon asked for an estimate for EU-hosted capacity (see attached spreadsheet).
- Data handling: PII redaction will be done client-side; Redwood will enable request-scoped KMS and audit logs for the trial.

Proposed evaluation plan (high-level):
1) Week 0 (kickoff): share sample prompt set (Lexicon) + Redwood provides baseline runs on candidate models.
2) Week 1: run 50k tokens/day across 2 models, collect latency and accuracy metrics; daily sync.
3) Week 2: refine prompts, enable prefix caching, run A/B with quantized variant for cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Week 3: final acceptance test (10 representative end-to-end workflows), documented acceptance checklist.

Immediate asks / next steps (owners):
- Maria (Lexicon): share canonical sample set (20–30 templates + 200 anonymized examples) by Wed 22 May.
- Ben (Redwood): provide instantiated regional token budget and recommended instance types by Tue 21 May (see attachment).
- Marcus (Redwood): prepare model variant matrix (inference cost, expected p50/p95 latency, recommended fallback routing) by Tue 21 May.
- Stephanie (Redwood): draft the POC SOW for signature, include data handling and SLAs, by Fri 24 May.

If that looks right I can turn this into a mutual action plan (MAP) in HubSpot and circulate.

—Olga

Thanks, Olga — appreciate the clear summary. Quick confirmations from our side:
- We'll target the 3-week window starting Mon 27 May.
- I'll share the anonymized sample set by EOD Wed 22 May (we're redacting PII first).
- The acceptance checklist aligns with our legal team's needs, but we'll flag any additional redaction checks during Week 1.

A few clarifying Qs:
1) For the fallback routing you suggested, can Redwood guarantee auto-fallback from Mistral-34B to Llama-3-13B-quant within 2s if p95 spikes? We need clear SLAs for degraded behavior.
2) On hallucination monitoring — can we get a daily report and the ability to upload manual blacklist terms to the evaluation harness?

Happy to sign the SOW when we see it. Also looping in procurement (<procurement@globex.com>) who will need an internal SOW copy.

—Maria

Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: POC decision log — regional token budget & model fallback matrix

Adding operational details for Maria's questions + notes from infra: 
- Auto-fallback timing: runtime routing policy can trigger within ~300–800ms (typical), and we can set a safe p95 trigger. We cannot "guarantee" sub-2s network-independent behavior, but we'll include a fallback SLA in the POC SOW that defines the expected degraded response window (max 2.5s) and an incident path.
- Daily hallucination report: yes — we'll generate a daily artifact (CSV + dashboard) with flagged responses. We will also add a one-click blacklist upload to the evaluation harness (max 500 terms during POC).
- Regional hosting: EU-only inference nodes (Frankfurt/Amsterdam). Token budget sheet assumes 50k tokens/day peak during the peak test; see 'regional_token_budget_estimate.xlsx' for cost breakdown.
- Model matrix highlights (short):
  * Mistral-Instruct-34B — highest quality, expected p50 ~180ms on rtx-a5000 equiv, cost medium-high.
  * Llama-3-13B-q4 — strong multilingual with smaller memory; good fallback for cost and latency.
  * opt-2.7b — degraded mode only (very low cost, higher hallucination risk).

Action: Marcus — can you produce the model variant CSV (fields: model_name, qps_estimate, p50_ms, p95_ms, est_cost_per_1k_tokens) by EOD Tue 21 May? I'll pull numbers into the SOW.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick status and owners to close this week so we can kick Mon 27 May as discussed: 
- Maria: sample set due Wed 22 May — noted.
- Marcus: model matrix CSV (Ben asked) — due today, please drop into the shared MAP doc.
- Ben: finalize token budget and instance-type recs — thanks for the sheet.
- Stephanie: SOW draft in HubSpot and GDrive by EOD Fri 24 May (include fallback SLA language).

I'll create the MAP and add explicit acceptance criteria rows (ex: "Extraction F1 >= 0.88 on holdout set"; "Hallucination < 3% across 100-sample manual audit"). Maria — once you confirm the sample set I will assign the "Acceptance Testing" step to Lexicon QA in the MAP.

If there are no objections I'll also propose the following default routing policy for the trial: primary -> Mistral-Instruct-34B (EU node); failover -> Llama-3-13B-q4 (quantized); degraded -> opt-2.7b with a forced low-confidence deferral to human review. We can tune thresholds during Week 1.

Thanks — will circulate the MAP link shortly.

—Olga
